Goal: make packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js take several files and stdin, for issue https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104. Deliver it as one pull request.

Context: the CLI currently takes one file (process.argv[2]), reads it with readFileSync, prints `${file}:${line}: ${error}` (newlines in the error replaced by spaces) for each problem from lint(text), and exits 0/1/2. Tests live in packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js (spawned CLI) and packages/jsonl-lint/test/lint.test.js. Zero dependencies, plain ES modules, node:test, Node 22+.

Steps:
1. Edit only packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js for behaviour. Do NOT touch packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js at all: lint(text) must stay byte-for-byte unchanged.
2. New CLI behaviour, `jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]`:
   - Check every named file in argument order. For each bad row print `<file>:<line>: <error>` on stdout, exactly the format used today for one file (file argument as given, newlines in the error replaced by a space). Output for each file is the same as running the tool on that file alone, concatenated in argument order.
   - An argument that is exactly `-` means read stdin (e.g. readFileSync(0, 'utf8')) and report its rows with the name `-` (e.g. `-:1: ...`).
   - If `-` appears more than once, it is a usage error: print a usage message on stderr and exit 2 (do this before checking any file).
   - No arguments: usage message on stderr, exit 2. Update the usage text to show `usage: jsonl-lint <file> [<file> ...]` and update the existing test in cli.test.js that matches the old usage text.
   - A file that can't be read: print `jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>: <message>` on stderr, keep going, and still check and report every other file.
   - Exit code: 2 if any file could not be read (or a usage error); otherwise 1 if any row in any file is bad; otherwise 0.
3. Add node:test tests in packages/jsonl-lint/test/cli.test.js (spawnSync the bin; pass stdin with the `input` option) covering at least, each as its own clearly named test:
   a. two clean files -> exit 0, empty stdout and stderr;
   b. one bad file among several clean ones -> exit 1, stdout has only that file's `<file>:<line>: ` lines, and order across several files follows argument order;
   c. stdin via `-`, clean input -> exit 0, no output;
   d. stdin via `-`, bad input -> exit 1, stdout lines start with `-:<line>: `;
   e. a missing file among good (and ideally one bad) files -> exit 2, stderr names the missing file, other files still checked and their bad rows still printed on stdout;
   f. two `-` arguments -> exit 2, message on stderr;
   g. no arguments -> exit 2, usage on stderr.
   Keep all existing tests passing.
4. Update packages/jsonl-lint/README.md: Usage section shows `node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...]`, explains that files are checked in order, that `-` reads stdin and is reported as `-`, that `-` may be given only once, and the exit codes (0 all clean, 1 any bad row in any file, 2 no file named / `-` twice / any file unreadable, with other files still checked).
5. Run `npm test` at the repository root and make it pass. Also sanity-check by hand, e.g. `printf '{bad}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js packages/jsonl-lint/package.json -; echo $?` (expect `-:1: ...` and exit 1).
6. Commit, push, and open exactly one pull request on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body contains the line `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`. Wait for the `test` workflow (.github/workflows/test.yml) to finish on the PR head and fix anything until it is green.
result.verifier:
Verify the pull request for https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104 at its head commit. Check out the PR head, run `npm ci` (or `npm install`) at the repository root, and run every command from the repository root. Run each multi-line block in a single shell invocation. Below, <PR> is the pull request number and <SHA> its head commit.

Setup (run once, before checks 1-3):
```
rm -rf /tmp/jlv && mkdir -p /tmp/jlv && printf '{"a":1}\n\n{"b":2}\n' > /tmp/jlv/c1.jsonl && printf '{"c":3}\n' > /tmp/jlv/c2.jsonl && printf '{"a":1}\n{bad}\n' > /tmp/jlv/b1.jsonl && printf 'nope\n{"x":1}\n{"torn":' > /tmp/jlv/b2.jsonl; echo setup=$?
```
(c1, c2 clean; b1 bad at line 2; b2 bad at lines 1 and 3.)

Check 1 — expect: "packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js <file> [<file> ...] checks every file named in order and prints <file>:<line>: <error> for each bad row, as for one file before"
Run:
```
B=packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js
diff <(node $B /tmp/jlv/b1.jsonl /tmp/jlv/c1.jsonl /tmp/jlv/b2.jsonl) <(node $B /tmp/jlv/b1.jsonl; node $B /tmp/jlv/b2.jsonl) && echo SAME-ORDERED
node $B /tmp/jlv/b1.jsonl /tmp/jlv/c1.jsonl /tmp/jlv/b2.jsonl; echo "exit=$?"
```
PASS: SAME-ORDERED is printed, and the second command prints exactly three lines: `/tmp/jlv/b1.jsonl:2: <error>`, `/tmp/jlv/b2.jsonl:1: <error>`, `/tmp/jlv/b2.jsonl:3: <error>` in that order, each with a non-empty JSON.parse error message. FAIL: diff output, any file skipped, wrong order, or a line not in `<file>:<line>: <error>` form.

Check 2 — expect: "A file named - is read from stdin and reported as -; a second - is a usage error (exit 2)"
Run:
```
printf '{bad}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js /tmp/jlv/c1.jsonl -; echo "exit=$?"
printf '{"a":1}\n' | node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js -; echo "exit=$?"
node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js - /tmp/jlv/c1.jsonl - </dev/null; echo "exit=$?"
```
PASS: first prints exactly one stdout line starting `-:1: ` and exit=1 (no `cannot read -` error); second prints nothing and exit=0; third prints a message on stderr and exit=2. FAIL: `-` treated as a file path, reported under another name, or the double `-` case not exiting 2.

Check 3 — expect: "Exit 0 if every file is clean, 1 if any row in any file is bad, 2 if no file is named or any file can't be read (error on stderr, other files still checked and reported)"
Run:
```
node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js /tmp/jlv/c1.jsonl /tmp/jlv/c2.jsonl; echo "exit=$?"
node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js /tmp/jlv/c1.jsonl /tmp/jlv/b1.jsonl; echo "exit=$?"
node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js; echo "exit=$?"
node packages/jsonl-lint/bin/jsonl-lint.js /tmp/jlv/c1.jsonl /tmp/jlv/missing.jsonl /tmp/jlv/b1.jsonl 2>/tmp/jlv/err.txt; echo "exit=$?"; cat /tmp/jlv/err.txt
```
PASS: exit=0 (no output); exit=1; exit=2 with a message on stderr; and for the last, exit=2, stderr names /tmp/jlv/missing.jsonl, and stdout still contains `/tmp/jlv/b1.jsonl:2: ` (the file after the missing one was checked and reported). FAIL: any other exit code, no stderr message, or b1's bad row missing from the last run.

Check 4 — expect: "lint(text) in src/index.js is unchanged"
Run:
```
git diff --exit-code b74bddb HEAD -- packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js; echo "diff-exit=$?"
```
(b74bddb is the commit before this work.) PASS: no diff output and diff-exit=0. FAIL: any change to packages/jsonl-lint/src/index.js.

Check 5 — expect: "node:test tests cover two clean files, one bad among several, stdin via - (clean and bad), a missing file among good ones, two - arguments and no arguments; the package README documents the usage"
Run:
```
npm test --workspace packages/jsonl-lint 2>&1 | tail -9
grep -n -e '<file> \[<file> \.\.\.\]' -e '`-`' -e 'stdin' packages/jsonl-lint/README.md
```
Then read packages/jsonl-lint/test/*.test.js. PASS: tests report `fail 0`, and there are node:test tests that run the CLI for each of: two clean files; one bad file among several; stdin via `-` with clean input; stdin via `-` with bad input; a missing file among good ones; two `-` arguments; no arguments — each asserting the exit code. The README documents multiple-file usage and `-` for stdin. FAIL: any test fails, any listed scenario has no test, or the README still shows only single-file usage.

Check 6 — expect: "The change is one PR on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test whose body says Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104, and npm test and the test workflow are green at its head"
Run:
```
gh api repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/pulls/<PR> --jq '.state, .head.sha, .body'
gh api repos/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/commits/<SHA>/check-runs --jq '.check_runs[] | [.name,.status,.conclusion] | @tsv'
npm test; echo "npm-exit=$?"
```
PASS: the PR is open on suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test, its body contains `Closes https://github.com/suredesigntshirts/ccp_machine_test/issues/104`, the `test` check run at <SHA> is completed with conclusion success, the local checkout is at <SHA>, and npm-exit=0. FAIL: body lacks that line, the work is split across PRs, the test check is missing/failed/pending, or npm test fails.

Advisory (not pass/fail):
- GitHub GraphQL may be blocked; use the REST `gh api` calls above rather than `gh pr view`.
- Note if unreadable-file errors are printed for `-` (stdin should never go through a path read).
- Note if the tests would still pass with the multi-file loop removed (weak assertions).
